correctness.rationale: For every prime p≥5 and smooth t²≠1, directly derive Cartier arrows on the holomorphic basis dx/y², x dx/y², dx/y. Establish all characteristic-dependent coefficient identities from the binomial-coefficient differential equation, its unique polynomial solution and evaluation of derivatives at t=1. Nonzero diagonal entries or a two-cycle retain rank through semilinear iteration, giving both p-rank and a-number. H_p has exact degree m with nonzero boundary values; its differential equation rules out repeated interior roots. The standalone verifier independently computes all identities and gcds for 18 primes, only as corroboration.

evidence: Nourozi–Rahmati arXiv:2306.07823 directly treats Cartier ranks generally but its congruence-only conclusion conflicts with the smooth p=11,t=0 exact zero matrix.

Laga–Shnidman arXiv:2308.15297 gives bielliptic Prym geometry without the stated characteristic-dependent parameter stratification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A known stronger theorem would cover the claimed strata even without naming this family. The closest general Cartier formulation supplies computational tools but does not establish a full exceptional parameter locus; the purported universal rank assertion is excluded by an explicit smooth counterexample. General L-polynomial algorithms and geometry theorems do not imply the formula.

originality.rationale: The closest primary bielliptic Picard paper introduces the exact family and its Prym theory but not p-rank/a-number strata. A general Picard Cartier paper gives coefficients and a congruence-only rank assertion contradicted by the smooth exact p=11,t=0 case; it therefore cannot subsume the exceptional root count. General Picard L-polynomial algorithms are broader in input but do not supply the specific all-primes parameter theorem. Mathematical-record, title, alias, family-parameter and related-statement comparisons found no stronger coverage. Residual risks explicitly recorded, not treated as novelty proof.
residual_risks: An unindexed older Cartier/Hasse divisor calculation in a differently normalized Picard pencil could predate this finding.
The closest general Picard rank preprint may have revised or restricted formulations not visible in the inspected material; the smooth p=11 exact counterexample is independently established.
A hypergeometric or Shimura-curve modular form could imply the separable Hasse polynomial by an equivalence not exposed in indexing.
The source match and novelty assessment are a self-review only; independent audit is outstanding.

value.rationale: A complete characteristic-uniform classification of two natural Jacobian invariants on the one-parameter bielliptic genus-three moduli family, not an arbitrary finite calculation. The explicit Hasse polynomial has precisely m simple smooth roots and determines exceptional rank-one or superspecial members; the uniform characteristic split, root count and concrete counterexamples fill a motivated gap in published Cartier and Prym work. No claim of full Newton polygons or independent certification is made.
